name: Jehoiakim
bio:
Eliakim, son of Josiah, was installed as king of Judah by Pharaoh-Necho of Egypt after Necho removed Eliakim's brother Jehoahaz; Necho renamed him Jehoiakim. He began to reign at twenty-five and reigned eleven years in Jerusalem; his mother was Zebudah, daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah. He taxed the people of Judah heavily to pay the silver and gold Pharaoh demanded as tribute, and did evil in the LORD's eyes like his ancestors (2 Kings 23:34-37).

## 📖 Core Story: Rebellion Against Babylon

Jehoiakim served Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, for three years before rebelling against him. In response, the LORD sent raiding bands of Chaldeans, Syrians, Moabites, and Ammonites against Judah — judgment for Manasseh's old sins and the innocent blood he had shed, which the LORD would not pardon. Jehoiakim died and was succeeded by his son Jehoiachin (2 Kings 24:1-6).
